rows.label: AB 1482 SF state-only cap
rows.notes: Does NOT apply to units under SF Rent Ordinance limits.

rows.label: State cap formula
rows.value: 5% + CPI or 10% lower; max two increases/12 months
rows.notes: CPI-U April-over-April, rounded nearest 0.1%, Aug. 1 cutoff.

rows.label: More-restrictive local exemption
rows.value: Units already subject to more restrictive local rent control are exempt from state cap

rows.label: Just cause
rows.value: Required after 12/24 months; lease expiration alone is not just cause

rows.label: Costa-Hawkins initial rent
rows.value: No limit on initial rent for vacant unit
rows.notes: Not a reset for existing tenancy.

rows.label: Costa-Hawkins d(2)
rows.value: Unlimited increase only to qualifying post-1995 lawful sublessee/assignee after original occupants no longer permanently reside

rows.label: Costa-Hawkins d(3)
rows.value: Partial occupancy changes protected when original occupant or qualifying pre-1996 lawful sublessee/assignee remains

rows.label: FEHA classes
rows.value: Race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran/military status, genetic information

rows.label: Exemption notices
rows.value: Required written notice for single-family/condo exemption; REIT/corporate/LLC limits

rows.label: Damages
rows.value: Injunctive relief, excess rent, attorney fees, up to treble for willful/oppressive/fraud/malice
rows.notes: State court enforcement; Rent Board cannot enforce state law.

rows.label: Retaliation - 180-day bar
rows.value: Where the tenant is not in default in rent, rent/service changes are barred within 180 days of the latest applicable enumerated tenantability event: good-faith notice/oral complaint to the landlord, bed-bug notice, qualifying recorded agency complaint, related inspection/citation, proceeding or adverse decision
rows.notes: Subdivision (a) may not be invoked more than once in 12 months. Subdivision (d) separately bars retaliation for organizing/lawful rights; (g) preserves lawful cause stated in good faith in the notice/pleading, subject to proof. Case timing is unverified.

rows.label: Retaliation - organizing and lawful rights
rows.value: Increasing rent to retaliate because a tenant organized or participated in a tenants' association, or lawfully exercised rights, is unlawful
rows.notes: The tenant bears the burden of producing evidence under this subdivision.

rows.label: Retaliation remedies
rows.value: Actual damages; $100-$2,000 punitive damages per retaliatory act only where fraud, oppression or malice is shown; in an action for damages for retaliatory eviction, reasonable attorney's fees to the prevailing party if requested upon initiation
rows.notes: Civil Code 1942.5(h)-(j); other statutory/decisional remedies are preserved. Not an automatic fee award for every rent-increase dispute.

rows.label: AB 1482 two-unit owner-occupied exemption
rows.value: Exempt only for a two-unit structure in a single building where the owner occupied one unit as a principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues in occupancy, and neither unit is an ADU/JADU
rows.notes: Owner occupancy of a unit here was not supplied; no exemption asserted (F34).

rows.label: AB 1482 separate-parcel exemption conditions
rows.value: Requires written tenant notice in the statutory form AND that the owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with at least one corporate member
rows.notes: An individual owner can meet the owner test, but the notice is still required.
